messages:
Marta: Quick dump from today's marketplace/procurement sync  they asked for a single-page policy that explains: commit bands, what counts toward the commit (cloud usage vs reserved GPUs vs SI invoices?), and explicit renewal remedies. We need one canonical answer.
Alex: Short answer: platform usage (metered tokens + reserved units) counts toward the commit. SI invoices do NOT count toward commit but are eligible for credit redemption. Hardware/appliance fees count only if the appliance SKU is in the private-offer.
Devon: Propose this definition block for the playbook: 
```
Commitable Spend = Redwood platform consumption (marketplace meter IDs listed in the PO) + reserved capacity SKUs referenced in the private-offer.
Excluded: one-time SI invoices, professional services, and 3rd-party appliance HW charges (unless appliance SKU included).
```
Priyanka: Procurement will press on renewals. Suggest two remediation paths if trailing 3mo utilization < 70%: (A) Customer opts for a 3mo ramp extension; OR (B) Customer accepts an applied credit equal to up to 40% of remaining vested smoothing credits (requires agreed remediation plan).
Marta: Good. Also add a "rollback" guard: if a customer repeatedly underutilizes (>2 consecutive terms < 65%), the CRO must approve renewal credits and the partner discount steps down by 3% unless a qualified growth plan is in place.
Alex: We should codify a non-stacking rule: private-offer credits cannot stack with public marketplace promo codes. Co-marketing incentives are separate and paid to the partner after joint milestones. Any stacking must be RevOps-approved.
Devon: Ops needs a reconciliation spec: monthly usage CSV (meter_id, customer_id, usage_units, billing_period) delivered within 7 business days of month-end; disputes logged within 45 days. Include required telemetry tag: private_offer_id.
Priyanka: For SI attachment, call out two separate flows: SI success payments (paid on milestone) and SI credit redemption (customer-facing credits that offset invoices). SI credits can be applied only after CSM sign-off of onboarding SLOs.
Marta: Example numbers to include in the one-pager (for procurement):
```
Commit band Bronze: >= $120k/yr -> 7% discount + $8k smoothing credit (vests monthly over 6mo)
Band Silver: >= $300k/yr -> 14% discount + $22k smoothing credit + SI success $12k
Band Gold: >= $800k/yr -> 20% discount + $60k smoothing credit + SI success $25k + early-renew bonus 3% if renewed >90d early
Renewal remedy: trailing 3mo avg usage < 70% -> choose 3mo extension OR apply up to 40% of smoothing credit to next term (with signed remediation plan). Repeat underutilization -> CRO review and possible discount step-down.
```
Alex: Legal will hate "refund" language. Phrase as "applied credit" or "fee waiver". Also require remediation plan documentation to unlock any smoothing-credit application.
Devon: Add SKU naming guidance: Private-offer SKU = "Redwood Commit (PrivOffer) - 1Y - <Band>". SI services as separate line: "Redwood SI - Onboarding (one-time)". Marketplace listing should surface a short attachment PDF with the commit definition and reconciliation cadence.
Priyanka: Announcement cadence: no marketplace publishing until SI toolkit, partner marketing assets, and RevOps meter mapping are live. Suggested timeline: 7 days post-close for joint partner announcement asset; 14 days post-close for marketplace private-offer publication.
Marta: Ops constraint: meter parity check in first billing cycle post-listing. If marketplace meter diverges >3% from internal meter, open immediate recon and pause credit vesting until resolved.
Alex: Also enforce discount floor: no discount below 5% without CRO sign-off. Good to state explicitly.
partner-bot: Created task: canonical-private-offer-playbook -> owner: Marta, due_in: 4 business days (id: PO-4415).
Devon: I'll draft the reconciliation CSV schema + sample file.
Priyanka: I'll draft the procurement FAQ with three calc scenarios (fast ramp, slow ramp, appliance included).
Alex: I'll loop in Legal and RevOps for word-smithing.
Marta: Thanks all. Once drafts land, we'll do a short review and ship the single-page playbook.
